settings.definition_quote: In the adversarial regime, by way of contrast to the stochastic regime, $( \ell_t  )_{t=1}^T$ is an arbitrary sequence. More precisely, $\ell_t$ can be chosen in an adversarial way depending on $(a_s)_{s=1}^{t-1}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic regime with adversarial corruption (linear bandits)
unmapped: noise need not be zero-mean nor identically distributed (Remark 3)
settings.definition_quote: It is parametrized by a true loss vector $\ell^* \in B_2^d(1)$ and by a \textit{corruption level} $C \geq 0$. In this regime, the sequence of $(\ell_t)_{t=1}^T$ is subject to the constraint that $\sum_{t=1}^T \| \ell_t - \ell^* \|_2 \leq C$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 (optimistic SCRiBLe-type FTRL with scaled-up sampling)

bound.expression_latex: d \sqrt{ \theta \log T (\min \{ Q, P \} + \E [ \sum_{t=1}^T (\varepsilon_t( a_t ))^2 ] ) } + d \theta \log T

tuning: psi is a theta-self-concordant barrier for conv(A)

source.label: thm:adv
source.quote: The regret for Algorithm~\ref{alg:FTRL} is bounded as R_T = O ( d \sqrt{ \theta \log T ( \min \{ Q, P \} + \E [ \sum_{t=1}^T (\varepsilon_t( a_t ))^2 ] ) } + d \theta \log T ).

results.notes: Q is quadratic variation min_lbar E sum ||l_t - lbar||^2 (mapped to Q_T). Valid for any choice of z_t; polynomial given barrier. Since Q <= T-ish, implies O(d sqrt(theta T log T)) when noise-free.

conditions: f_t(a) >= 0 for all a in A and t

source.label: thm:adv
source.quote: Further, if $f_t(a) \geq 0$ for any $a \in \cA$ and $t \in [T]$, we have R_T = O ( d \sqrt{ \theta L^* \log T } + d \theta \log T ).

results.notes: First-order bound; L* = min_a E[sum f_t(a)].

symbols.Sigma_sum: sum_t sigma_t^2 with sigma_t^2 = max_a E[eps_t(a)^2]

source.label: thm:sto
source.quote: We have R_T = O( d \sqrt{ ( C + \sum_{t=1}^T \sigma_{t}^2 ) \theta \log T } + d \theta \log T), where we define $\sigma_{t}^2 = \max_{a \in \cA} \E [ (\varepsilon_t(a))^2 ]$.

results.notes: Does not require assumption on z_t.

bound.expression_latex: ( \frac{\kappa d \sigma^2}{\Delta_{\min}} + 1 ) d\theta \log T + \sqrt{ ( \frac{ \kappa \sigma^2}{\Delta_{\min}}  + 1 ) C d^2 \theta \log T }

symbols.kappa: approximation factor of the reference point z_t in (eq:aspzt), kappa >= 1
symbols.sigma_sq_max: max_t max_a E[eps_t(a)^2] (maximum noise second moment)

tuning: z_t chosen so that r_t <= kappa * min_z max_{x in E_t} pi_{z,X}(x)

source.label: thm:sto
source.quote: Further, if $a^* \in \argmin_{a \in \cA} \linner \ell^*, a \rinner$ exists uniquely, under the assumption of \eqref{eq:aspzt}, we have R_T (a^*) = O( ( \frac{\kappa d \sigma^2}{\Delta_{\min}} + 1 ) d\theta \log T + \sqrt{ ( \frac{ \kappa \sigma^2}{\Delta_{\min}}  + 1 ) C d^2 \theta \log T } )

results.notes: With C=0 gives stochastic bound O((d sigma^2/Delta_min + 1) d theta log T). Computing z_t naively takes O(poly(d)|A|) time, possibly exponential in d. Regret includes corruption.
